q: A biological molecule (biomolecule) is a chemical compound that naturally occurs in ____.
e: A biological molecule (biomolecule) is a chemical compound that naturally occurs in living organisms. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock.

q: Carbon is an element present in all organic biological ____.
e: Carbon is an element present in all organic biological molecules. Organic biological molecules all contain carbon.

q: Other elements always present are oxygen and hydrogen. Nitrogen is sometimes ____.
e: Other elements always present are oxygen and hydrogen. Nitrogen is sometimes present. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: When macromolecules are made of long chains of monomers held together by chemical bonds, they are known as ____.
e: When macromolecules are made of long chains of monomers held together by chemical bonds, they are known as polymers. Polymers are long chains of repeating monomers.

q: Examples are carbohydrates, proteins and nucleic acids. Lipids are not polymers but important ____.
e: Examples are carbohydrates, proteins and nucleic acids. Lipids are not polymers but important biomolecule. A biomolecule is a chemical that occurs naturally in living organisms. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: Water is the most important biochemical of all living ____.
e: Water is the most important biochemical of all living things. Things is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Water is a major component of cells, typically forming between 70% and 95 % of the ____.
e: Water is a major component of cells, typically forming between 70% and 95 % of the cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Water typically makes up about 70 to 95 percent of a cell.

q: About 60% present in ____.
e: About 60% present in human. Human is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Water molecules have two poles i.e. a positive hydrogen pole and a negative oxygen pole, it is termed as polarity and water is a ____ molecule.
e: Water molecules have two poles i.e. A positive hydrogen pole and a negative oxygen pole, it is termed as polarity and water is a polar molecule. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: A bond called hydrogen bond (H-bond), which formed in liquid state of water providing useful and significant properties of water in the living ____.
e: A bond called hydrogen bond (H-bond), which formed in liquid state of water providing useful and significant properties of water in the living organisms. Hydrogen bonds between water molecules give cohesion, solvent power, and thermal buffering. Hydrogen bonds form because oxygen in water is slightly negative and hydrogen is slightly positive.

q: Water has a high specific heat. Specific heat is the amount of heat that must be absorbed in order for 1 g of a substance to change its temperature ____ ℃.
e: Water has a high specific heat. Specific heat is the amount of heat that must be absorbed in order for 1 g of a substance to change its temperature 1 ℃. Water absorbs a lot of heat with little temperature change, so it buffers cells.

q: Water has a high heat of ____.
e: Water has a high heat of vaporization. Water's high heat of vaporization makes sweating and transpiration effective coolants.

q: Water is the universal ____.
e: Water is the universal solvent. Solvent is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Water exhibits strong cohesion ____.
e: Water exhibits strong cohesion tension. Cohesion is water molecules sticking to each other by hydrogen bonds.

q: Water moves up a tall tree from the roots to the leaves without the expenditure of energy by what is referred to as transpirational-pull and/or ____ tension.
e: Water moves up a tall tree from the roots to the leaves without the expenditure of energy by what is referred to as transpirational-pull and/or cohesion tension. Cohesion is water molecules sticking to each other by hydrogen bonds. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low.

q: Strong cohesion also results in surface tension that allows insects to walk on water without breaking the ____.
e: Strong cohesion also results in surface tension that allows insects to walk on water without breaking the surface. Cohesion is water molecules sticking to each other by hydrogen bonds. Many insects breathe through a tracheal system, not lungs.

q: Water has high adhesion ____.
e: Water has high adhesion properties. Properties is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Adhesion is an attraction between two different ____.
e: Adhesion is an attraction between two different molecules. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Density or specific gravity of water is highest at ____℃.
e: Density or specific gravity of water is highest at 4 ℃. 4 is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Carbohydrates are organic molecules composed of carbon(C), hydrogen(H) and ____ (O).
e: Carbohydrates are organic molecules composed of carbon(C), hydrogen(H) and oxygen (O). Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: Carbohydrates mainly originated from ____ materials.
e: Carbohydrates mainly originated from plant materials. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: Carbohydrates are divided into three groups: namely monosaccharides (simple sugars), disaccharides and ____.
e: Carbohydrates are divided into three groups: namely monosaccharides (simple sugars), disaccharides and polysaccharides. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: Monosaccharides are simple sugars in which there is one oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms for each carbon atom in the ____.
e: Monosaccharides are simple sugars in which there is one oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms for each carbon atom in the molecule. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: A general formula for this can be written ____.
e: A general formula for this can be written (CH₂O)ₙ. (CH₂O)ₙ is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Triose sugars (n=3) have three carbon atoms and the general formula C₃H₆O₃, such as glycerol, glyceraldehyde and ____.
e: Triose sugars (n=3) have three carbon atoms and the general formula C₃H₆O₃, such as glycerol, glyceraldehyde and dihydroxyacetone. Glycerol combines with fatty acids to make a triglyceride. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: They are important in mitochondria, where the respiration process breaks down glucose into ____ sugars.
e: They are important in mitochondria, where the respiration process breaks down glucose into triose sugars. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Pentose sugars(n=5) have five carbon atoms and the general formula C₅H₁₀O₅. Ribose and deoxyribose are important pentose sugars in the nucleic acids ribonucleic acid (RNA) and deoxyribonucleic acid (____).
e: Pentose sugars(n=5) have five carbon atoms and the general formula C₅H₁₀O₅. Ribose and deoxyribose are important pentose sugars in the nucleic acids ribonucleic acid (RNA) and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Deoxyribose is the sugar in DNA.

q: Hexose sugars(n=6) have six carbon atoms and the general formula ____.
e: Hexose sugars(n=6) have six carbon atoms and the general formula C₆H₁₂O₆. C₆H₁₂O₆ is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Ring structure has two isomers (different forms): α and β such as α-glucose and ____-glucose.
e: Ring structure has two isomers (different forms): α and β such as α-glucose and β -glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Most living things create energy by breaking down the monosaccharide '____' and harvest the energy released from chemical bonds of glucose.
e: Most living things create energy by breaking down the monosaccharide ' glucose ' and harvest the energy released from chemical bonds of glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Disaccharides are made up of two monosaccharides joined together by a ____ linkage.
e: Disaccharides are made up of two monosaccharides joined together by a glycosidic linkage. A glycosidic bond joins sugar units in disaccharides and polysaccharides. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Maltose is made up of two glucose units joined: found in germinating seed such as ____.
e: Maltose is made up of two glucose units joined: found in germinating seed such as barley. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms.

q: Sucrose, a table sugar is made up of one glucose molecule joined with one ____ molecule.
e: Sucrose, a table sugar is made up of one glucose molecule joined with one fructose molecule. Fructose is an isomer of glucose found in many fruits. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Lactose, a milk sugar is made up of one galactose unit joined with one ____.
e: Lactose, a milk sugar is made up of one galactose unit joined with one glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Polysaccharides are formed by many monosaccharides units joined together by ____ bonds.
e: Polysaccharides are formed by many monosaccharides units joined together by covalent bonds. Covalent is the biological term this statement needs.

q: They are insoluble and serve as reserve food and ____ materials.
e: They are insoluble and serve as reserve food and structural materials. Structural is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Cellulose is a polysaccharide made up of several molecules of glucose joined by ____ glycosidic linkages.
e: Cellulose is a polysaccharide made up of several molecules of glucose joined by β1-4 glycosidic linkages. A glycosidic bond joins sugar units in disaccharides and polysaccharides. Cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid.

q: It is the main component of cell wall in ____.
e: It is the main component of cell wall in plants. Plants is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Starch is made up of millions of glucose molecules by ____ process of green plants.
e: Starch is made up of millions of glucose molecules by photosynthesis process of green plants. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: The basic chemical formula of the starch molecule is ____.
e: The basic chemical formula of the starch molecule is (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ. Starch is the plant storage polysaccharide made of amylose and amylopectin.

q: It is composed of two portions: (i) Amylose—linear portion containing glucose units joined by ____ glycosidic linkages.
e: It is composed of two portions: (i) Amylose—linear portion containing glucose units joined by α1-4 glycosidic linkages. A glycosidic bond joins sugar units in disaccharides and polysaccharides. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Its content in starch is about ____%.
e: Its content in starch is about 20 %. Starch is the plant storage polysaccharide made of amylose and amylopectin.

q: Amylopectin is a branched chain polymer of glucose units joined by α1-4 glycosidic linkages as well as by ____ glycosidic linkages.
e: Amylopectin is a branched chain polymer of glucose units joined by α1-4 glycosidic linkages as well as by α1-6 glycosidic linkages. A glycosidic bond joins sugar units in disaccharides and polysaccharides. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Its content in starch is about ____%.
e: Its content in starch is about 20 %. Starch is the plant storage polysaccharide made of amylose and amylopectin.

q: Glycogen is made up of millions of glucose molecules and formed the main storage ____.
e: Glycogen is made up of millions of glucose molecules and formed the main storage carbohydrate. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals.

q: It is found in animal and ____.
e: It is found in animal and fungi. Fungi is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In mammals, glycogen molecules are stored in the liver and ____ cells.
e: In mammals, glycogen molecules are stored in the liver and muscle cells. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals. The liver stores glycogen, makes bile, and handles many blood chemicals.

q: Lipids are another group of important biological molecules present in all cellular organisms and some ____.
e: Lipids are another group of important biological molecules present in all cellular organisms and some viruses. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell.

q: Structurally, most lipids (triglycerides) consist of one glycerol join with three ____.
e: Structurally, most lipids (triglycerides) consist of one glycerol join with three fatty acids. Fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains that may be saturated or unsaturated. Glycerol combines with fatty acids to make a triglyceride.

q: Glycerol is a three carbons simple ____.
e: Glycerol is a three carbons simple alcohol. Glycerol combines with fatty acids to make a triglyceride. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: Fatty acids present in simple lipids are generally made up of 12 to ____ carbon atoms.
e: Fatty acids present in simple lipids are generally made up of 12 to 22 carbon atoms. Fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains that may be saturated or unsaturated. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers.

q: Animal lipids are often saturated fats, which causes problem in human health except in ____ oil.
e: Animal lipids are often saturated fats, which causes problem in human health except in fish oil. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers.

q: Plant lipids are often unsaturated fats, which promote human ____.
e: Plant lipids are often unsaturated fats, which promote human health. Medicine and veterinary science restore and maintain health. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers.

q: Lipids contain more energy per gram than ____.
e: Lipids contain more energy per gram than carbohydrates. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers.

q: A layer of fat under the skin reduces heat ____.
e: A layer of fat under the skin reduces heat loss. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Lipids are less dense than water so, help animals to ____.
e: Lipids are less dense than water so, help animals to float. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers.

q: Proteins are naturally occurring macromolecules formed by joining many amino acids with ____ bonds.
e: Proteins are naturally occurring macromolecules formed by joining many amino acids with peptide bonds. A peptide bond joins the carboxyl of one amino acid to the amine of the next. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: Amino acids are the simplest units of protein and form the building blocks of ____.
e: Amino acids are the simplest units of protein and form the building blocks of proteins. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: It is made of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and ____.
e: It is made of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: The peptide bond is a covalent bond, which is formed between the amine group (-NH₂) from one amino acid and the carboxyl group (-COOH) of ____.
e: The peptide bond is a covalent bond, which is formed between the amine group (-NH₂) from one amino acid and the carboxyl group (-COOH) of another. A peptide bond joins the carboxyl of one amino acid to the amine of the next.

q: There are about ____ different naturally occurring amino acids.
e: There are about 20 different naturally occurring amino acids. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: Proteins are synthesized at ____ of living cells.
e: Proteins are synthesized at ribosomes of living cells. Ribosomes assemble proteins; they are not the site of photosynthesis. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Primary structure is simply the linear sequence of amino acids linked into a ____ chain.
e: Primary structure is simply the linear sequence of amino acids linked into a polypeptide chain. A polypeptide is a chain of amino acids; a protein may have one or more chains. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: Secondary structure forms folded structures within a polypeptide due to interactions between atoms of the backbone of ____.
e: Secondary structure forms folded structures within a polypeptide due to interactions between atoms of the backbone of amino acids. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon. A polypeptide is a chain of amino acids; a protein may have one or more chains.

q: The most common types of secondary structures are the α-helix and the ____ sheet.
e: The most common types of secondary structures are the α-helix and the β-pleated sheet. Β-pleated is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Tertiary structure is primarily due to interactions between the R groups of the amino acids that make up the ____.
e: Tertiary structure is primarily due to interactions between the R groups of the amino acids that make up the protein. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: Some globular proteins consist of two or more polypeptide chains. This complex large molecule is referred to the ____ structure.
e: Some globular proteins consist of two or more polypeptide chains. This complex large molecule is referred to the quaternary structure. A polypeptide is a chain of amino acids; a protein may have one or more chains. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: When beyond the optimum temperature, the cross-linkages in protein molecules break down: the protein molecules lost their shape and will not usually regain it even when cooled. This protein is said to have been ____.
e: When beyond the optimum temperature, the cross-linkages in protein molecules break down: the protein molecules lost their shape and will not usually regain it even when cooled. This protein is said to have been denatured. A denatured enzyme has lost its shape, so the active site no longer works. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: The egg white protein, albumin has been denatured by ____.
e: The egg white protein, albumin has been denatured by heat. A denatured enzyme has lost its shape, so the active site no longer works. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Enzymes are mostly proteins, which are able to act as catalysts in ____ reactions.
e: Enzymes are mostly proteins, which are able to act as catalysts in biochemical reactions. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: Enzymes remain unchanged after the ____.
e: Enzymes remain unchanged after the reaction. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: Many enzyme names end in-____ for example amylase, lipase and protease.
e: Many enzyme names end in- ase for example amylase, lipase and protease. Proteases digest proteins to amino acids. Amylase is the enzyme that hydrolyses starch.

q: A small area on the surface of an enzyme is called the ____ site.
e: A small area on the surface of an enzyme is called the active site. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: The specific binding of enzyme molecule and the substrate molecule are regarded as "____ and key model".
e: The specific binding of enzyme molecule and the substrate molecule are regarded as " lock and key model". The lock-and-key idea says the substrate fits the active site by shape. The substrate is the molecule the enzyme acts on.

q: A cofactor is a non-protein chemical compound or metallic ion that assists in an enzyme's activity as a ____.
e: A cofactor is a non-protein chemical compound or metallic ion that assists in an enzyme's activity as a catalyst. A catalyst speeds a reaction and is not consumed by it. Most enzymes are proteins.

q: Cofactors can be divided into two types: inorganic cofactor and organic cofactor called ____.
e: Cofactors can be divided into two types: inorganic cofactor and organic cofactor called coenzyme. A coenzyme is an organic cofactor, often made from a vitamin. Inorganic substances may lack carbon chains; they are not the carbon-based macromolecules of cells.

q: The coenzyme NAD (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide) used in the respiration comes from nicotinic acid, a member of the vitamin ____ complex.
e: The coenzyme NAD (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide) used in the respiration comes from nicotinic acid, a member of the vitamin B complex. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. A coenzyme is an organic cofactor, often made from a vitamin.

q: Nucleic acids are hereditary biomolecules which are essential to all known forms of ____.
e: Nucleic acids are hereditary biomolecules which are essential to all known forms of life. Biology is the science of life: plants, animals, and microorganisms. Nucleic acids DNA and RNA store and transfer genetic information.

q: Viruses also have ____ acid.
e: Viruses also have nucleic acid. Nucleic acids DNA and RNA store and transfer genetic information. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell.

q: Nucleic acids contain the same elements as proteins: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and ____.
e: Nucleic acids contain the same elements as proteins: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and phosphorous. Nitrogen bases make nitrogen essential in DNA and RNA. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: The two main types of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (____).
e: The two main types of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA). RNA is the nucleic acid that helps turn DNA information into protein. Nucleic acids DNA and RNA store and transfer genetic information.

q: DNA encodes the information the cell needs to make ____.
e: DNA encodes the information the cell needs to make proteins. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: Nucleic acids are composed of several molecules of ____.
e: Nucleic acids are composed of several molecules of nucleotides. Nucleotides are the monomers of DNA and RNA. Nucleic acids DNA and RNA store and transfer genetic information.

q: Each nucleotide contains a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a ____ group.
e: Each nucleotide contains a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group. A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogen base.

q: The two carbon-nitrogen rings bases (adenine and guanine) are purines, while the one carbon-nitrogen ring bases (thymine and cytosine) are ____.
e: The two carbon-nitrogen rings bases (adenine and guanine) are purines, while the one carbon-nitrogen ring bases (thymine and cytosine) are pyrimidines. Pyrimidines are the single-ring bases cytosine, thymine, and uracil. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: RNA has the nucleobase uracil, which is substituted for thymine in ____.
e: RNA has the nucleobase uracil, which is substituted for thymine in DNA. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Uracil replaces thymine in RNA.
